what: [order-path] order_monitor's strategy+symbol fallback can bind a package to ANOTHER package's trade once per-account packages coexist. src/runtime/order_monitor.py (package-leg resolver, ~L828-858): when an open package has no package-scoped open trade rows AND no linked_trade_id, it falls back to _find_trade_by_match(strategy, symbol) -> the most recent open trade for that strategy+symbol, on ANY package, and effectuates this package's verdict (trail/close) against it. Until #14590 two open packages for one strategy+symbol were rare (the gate was strategy-wide). With the per-account/pair-coupled gate (#14590) they coexist routinely: e.g. a Stage-1 soak package on alpaca_paper plus a Stage-2 package on alpaca_live/alpaca_portfolio for the same leg. A package that loses its legs without a linked id could then trail or close the other package's trade. Not measured on live data yet: how many open packages today have linked_trade_id NULL and no open rows.
why_it_matters: A wrong-package match can move the stop on, or close, a real-money leg on the strength of a different package's exit verdict.
